                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure can lead to damage of cranial nerves III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), VI (abducens), and V1 (ophthalmic branch of trigeminal nerve). This can result in absent left corneal reflex due to sensory loss from V1 involvement, as well as impaired lateral gaze due to CN VI involvement. The presence of left periorbital ecchymosis suggests potential trauma to the area, supporting the likelihood of cranial nerve involvement. Therefore, the most likely physical examination finding is absent left corneal reflex (option opd). Other options, such as complete loss of vision (option ope) and preserved left lateral gaze (option opc), are less likely based on the known anatomy and function of the affected nerves.
